title: Consolidate FixedTimeEquals into shared helper (3 copies → 1)
description:
P1: Three independent implementations of the same length-leaking timing-safe comparison pattern exist: `MemorySmithRequestGuardMiddleware.cs:98-110`, `SecurityServices.cs:337-349`, `SecurityServices.cs:799-804`. All three share the identical flaw: `actualBytes.Length == expectedBytes.Length && CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals(...)` — the `&&` short-circuits on length mismatch before reaching the constant-time compare, leaking key length via response timing. Practical impact is LOW (keys are 32+ bytes of entropy), but the pattern is proven to propagate by copy-paste (2→3 copies).

Scope:
- Create `SecurityCompare.FixedTimeEquals(string, string)` in `MemorySmith.Core` (pad-to-common-length internally, no short-circuit)
- Delete all 3 private copies
- Add tests for the shared helper

Evidence: MemorySmith-Audit-20260702.md §1.5, council/audit-synthesis-council-20260705.md

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from 6-seat council audit synthesis. Source-Grounded Archivist confirmed all 3 copies at 97% confidence. Skeptical Reviewer agreed LOW severity but noted the copy-paste propagation pattern is itself a finding.
